findings.title: Same concurrent-delete NPE remains in the paginated getSubGroupsStream overloads
findings.body:
The PR null-guards `modelSupplier.get()` only in `getSubGroupsCount()`. Three sibling methods still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` with no null check:
- `getSubGroupsStream(search, firstResult, maxResults)` (line 256)
- `getSubGroupsStream(firstResult, maxResults)` (line 262)
- `getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, firstResult, maxResults)` (line 268)

`getGroupById` on the delegate returns null once the group is deleted in the database while the cached adapter is still in use. In that window these methods throw the same NullPointerException the PR is meant to fix. A realistic trigger is listing a group's children (the admin console's children endpoint) while another request deletes the group. The fix is incomplete; these methods should get the same null handling, e.g. return `Stream.empty()`.

findings.title: Reader thread is never joined, so exceptions can be missed and the thread leaks
findings.body:
After the deletes, the test sets `deletedAll` to true and immediately asserts that `caughtExceptions` is empty. It never waits for the reader thread to finish.

The reader may still be inside a `groups()` request at that moment. That last request is the one most likely to hit the race, and any exception from it is added after the assertion has already passed, so the regression can go undetected.

The thread is also non-daemon and unmanaged. It can keep sending requests to the shared managed realm while cleanup or the next test runs, which causes cross-test interference.

Keep a reference to the thread and `join()` it (with a timeout) before asserting.

findings.title: Test does not ensure reads actually overlap with deletes
findings.body:
The reader thread is started and the main thread begins deleting right away. Nothing guarantees the reader has started, or completed any request, before or during the deletions. On a fast or loaded machine the deletes can finish before any concurrent read happens, and the test passes without exercising the fix.

A latch or counter would fix this, for example:
- wait for the first successful read before starting deletes, and/or
- assert that at least N reads happened while deletes were in progress.

Without it, the regression test is nondeterministic and can pass vacuously.

findings.title: getSubGroupsCount now returns null, unlike other GroupModel implementations
findings.body:
Other `GroupModel` implementations return an actual count and never null: the default method counts the subgroup stream, and JPA runs a count query. The cached adapter now returns `null` when the backing group has disappeared. Any caller that unboxes or compares the `Long` (e.g. `getSubGroupsCount() > 0`) would trade the original NPE for a new one.

Returning `0L` for a deleted group would keep the contract consistent. Alternatively, document that null means "group no longer exists".

findings.title: Hierarchy population still NPEs if a parent group is deleted concurrently
findings.body:
`populateGroupHierarchyFromSubGroups` looks up each parent with `session.groups().getGroupById(realm, currGroup.getParentId())` and uses the result without a null check. The result is passed to `groupEvaluator.canView(parentModel)`, `toRepresentation(groupEvaluator, parentModel, full)` and `populateSubGroupCount(parentModel, parent)`.

This code path runs when groups are searched. If a parent is deleted between loading the child and walking up the tree, the lookup returns null and the request fails with a NullPointerException. This is the same class of bug the PR addresses, and this file is touched by the PR, but the path is left unguarded. The new test only covers the non-search listing, so it does not catch it.
